note: Replicas are independent chains, so the split is statistically exact but not bit-identical: the RNG keys differ. On one GPU the two launches are serial, so the wall clock of the protocol is their sum.

analysis.question: Does the split protocol (51+49, width 1 each) beat the current production convention (50+50, width 2 each)? Both are two launches of 100 replicas total, so the fixed launch cost is paid twice in BOTH, and the only variable left is vector width 1 against width 2.

answer.reading: 51+49 is 0.76% SLOWER than 50+50, which is inside the measurement's own resolution. Width 2 is free, now confirmed with launch count held fixed. The protocol gains nothing over the current convention at this size.

my_prediction_was_wrong.basis: the 52-point survey put B=50 at 9.788 s/replica against 9.130 at B=45 and 9.162 at B=55, i.e. 7.0% high, which I attributed to the sawtooth
my_prediction_was_wrong.why_wrong: B=50's +7% in the survey did not reproduce. The survey used short cells, where we have since measured +-2.5% noise in both directions, and a single run. The anomaly that made my B=50 interpolation fail by 7% was most likely that noise, not a real feature of the curve at B=50.
my_prediction_was_wrong.lesson: a single short-cell point is not evidence of a sawtooth feature below ~5%

model_validated_out_of_sample.model: W(B) = a + b*B with a = 0.0820 s, b = 0.007215 s/replica
model_validated_out_of_sample.fitted_on: the PREVIOUS run (split_protocol.json), not on this one
model_validated_out_of_sample.verdict: every width-1 and width-2 config predicted within 1.5%, out of sample

width4_penalty_isolated.note: a clean single number for the width-4 penalty, against the validated model

what_actually_dominates_here.finding: At this scale the LAUNCH COUNT matters far more than the width.
what_actually_dominates_here.reading: For 100 replicas a SINGLE odd batch of 99 or 101 beats either two-launch option by 8 to 10%, because it pays the fixed cost once instead of twice.

the_practical_consequence_for_200.note: extrapolated with the model validated above, not measured directly
the_practical_consequence_for_200.reading: If production currently runs one launch per state, 4 states x 50 replicas is FOUR launches. The protocol's 101+99 is TWO, and beats it by 9.3% -- by launch count, not by width. The protocol's real value is not that it reaches width 1; it is that it reaches 200 replicas in two launches instead of four, while avoiding the width-4 batch.

limits: One H100, 3600 sweeps, nine interleaved repeats, dispersion 0.1-0.2%.
The 200-replica row is modelled, not measured; only the 100-replica rows are direct measurements here.
Everything is the width axis. The sawtooth is untouched: B=99 and B=101 differ by 2.3% and both are width 1.
